renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: cluster_size_profile
  title: Initial cluster sizes
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the number of MMseqs2 clusters of every size before families are built. It answers how the input sequences group and how many clusters are large enough to seed a family.
    How to read: most clusters are tiny, so the curve falls steeply and the count axis is logarithmic. Only the tail to the right of the line can become families, so a sample with almost nothing there will yield few families. Lower the threshold to get more families.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line at 25 is the default minimum cluster size of nf-core/proteinfamilies for seeding a family. The run may have set another value, which this tile does not read.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: profile
  config:
    log_y: true
    reference_x: 25
    reference_label: Default minimum cluster size (25)
    x_title: Sequences in the cluster
    y_title: Clusters
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: cluster_size
    y: n_clusters

- component: card
  id: clusters_total
  title: Initial clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of clusters over the samples in view, and the second number is the count in the most populated size class. It answers how finely the input fell apart.
    How to read: the singletons dominate nearly every run, so the largest class is usually the one of size one. Compare with the tail in the profile to see how many clusters can seed a family.
  column: n_clusters
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: clusters, with the largest size class

- component: figure
  id: sequence_share_bar
  title: Share of sequences by cluster size
  description: |-
    Each bar is a cluster size: the share of a sample's input sequences that sit in clusters of that size. It answers how much of the input is clustered into groups large enough to be useful.
    How to read: a tall bar at size one means most sequences are unclustered. Mass further right means the sample holds many related sequences that can form families.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_size
    y: sequence_share
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      cluster_size: Sequences in the cluster
      sequence_share: Share of the sample's sequences
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Cluster size table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and cluster size with the number of clusters, the sequences they hold and their share of the sample. It answers the exact numbers behind the profile and the bars.
    How to read: sort by cluster size to read the tail that can seed families.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: member_scatter
  title: Member coverage against identity
  description: |-
    Each point is a member sequence of a family: the share of the representative it covers against its identity to the representative, coloured by whether the family is new or an updated existing one and sized by length. It answers which members are fragments and which are divergent.
    How to read: well-behaved members sit top right. Fragments sit to the left, and divergent members, which may be false recruits, sit low. The pipeline recruits only members covering at least 90% of the family model length by default, so a member far left deserves a look.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Share of the representative covered
    y_title: Identity to the representative
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: coverage
    y: identity
    label: member_id
    color: origin
    size: length

- component: card
  id: members_count
  title: Family members
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of members over the families in view, and the second number is the count of families. It answers how many sequences the families hold.
    How to read: divide the members by the families to get the average family size. Filter to one family to list its members in the table.
  column: family
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: members, with the families they belong to

- component: card
  id: member_identity
  title: Member identity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median identity of members to their family representative, and the box shows the spread. It answers how similar the members are to the representative.
    How to read: families built from distant homologs are expected to have a modest identity, since the clustering identity default is low. A long box means some members are far from the representative.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: member_coverage
  title: Member coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of the representative that members cover, and the box shows the spread. It answers how complete the members are.
    How to read: values near one mean members span the whole family. A long lower tail means fragments, which the scatter shows one by one.
  column: coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: member_length
  title: Member length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ungapped length of members in residues, and the box shows the spread. It answers how long the family sequences are.
    How to read: lengths within one family should be close. Filter to a family to check that, since pooled families of different domains differ widely.
  column: length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: identity_box
  title: Member identity per family
  description: |-
    Each box is a family: the spread of its members' identity to the representative, coloured by whether the family is new or updated. It answers which families are tight and which are diverse.
    How to read: a high, short box is a tight family. A low or long box is a diverse one, a candidate for a split or a second look.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median identity to the representative of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: family
    y: identity
    color: origin
    labels:
      family: Family
      identity: Identity to the representative
      origin: Origin
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: identity

- component: table
  title: Family member table
  description: |-
    Each row is a member sequence with its family, origin, identity, coverage and length. It answers the exact values behind the scatter and the cards.
    How to read: filter to a family and sort by coverage to list its fragments.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: family_landscape
  title: Family size against conservation
  description: |-
    Each point is a family: its number of member sequences against the mean conservation of its residues, coloured by whether it is new or an updated existing family and sized by the representative length. It answers which families are big and which are well conserved.
    How to read: big families spread to the right. A low point is a family whose members agree on few residues, a candidate for a second look or a split. A small, highly conserved family is a tight group of close homologs.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median mean residue conservation of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Member sequences
    y_title: Mean residue conservation
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: size
    y: mean_conservation
    label: family
    color: origin
    size: representative_length

- component: card
  id: families_total
  title: Protein families
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of families built or updated, and the second number is the count of samples they come from. It answers how many families the run produced.
    How to read: few families from a large input usually means the minimum cluster size was high. Lower it to get more families.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: families, with the samples they come from
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: members_total
  title: Family members
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of member sequences over all families, and the second number is the size of the largest family. It answers how many sequences the families hold and how skewed they are.
    How to read: a largest family far above the average means one family dominates. Open the scatter to see how the others spread.
  column: size
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: members, with the largest family
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: family_size
  title: Family size
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median number of member sequences per family, with the smallest and largest family beside it. It answers how big a typical family is and how wide the range is.
    How to read: sizes span a wide range, so a median close to the minimum means many small families and a few big ones.
  column: size
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the smallest and largest

- component: card
  id: representative_length
  title: Representative length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median length of the family representatives in residues, and the box shows the spread. It answers how long the proteins of the families are.
    How to read: short representatives are often single domains and long ones multi-domain proteins or fragments. A very short value can mark fragmentary families.
  column: representative_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: family_identity
  title: Family identity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of each family's mean identity of members to the representative, and the box shows the spread. It answers how similar the family members are.
    How to read: the pipeline clusters distant homologs by default, with a minimum identity of 0.3, so modest values are expected. A family far below its peers may merge unrelated sequences.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: mean_identity
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: family_conservation
  title: Family conservation
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of each family's mean residue conservation along the representative, and the box shows the spread. It answers how well the alignments agree column by column.
    How to read: higher means more conserved families. Low values point to diverse or poorly aligned families worth a second look.
  column: mean_conservation
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: recruited_total
  title: Recruited members
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of members added beyond the seed sequences, and the second number is the largest recruitment into one family. It answers how much the family models gained after the first clustering.
    How to read: recruits are found by searching the model against the input, with a minimum length filter of 90% of the model by default. A family with a large recruitment grew far beyond its seed.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/nextflow_schema.json
  column: recruited
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: recruits, with the largest family

- component: figure
  id: family_size_box
  title: Family size per sample
  description: |-
    Each box is a sample: the spread of its family sizes on a logarithmic scale, coloured by whether families are new or updated. It answers how family sizes compare between samples.
    How to read: compare the medians and the whiskers. A sample with only small families had little redundancy in its input.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median family size of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the pipeline.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: size
    color: origin
    log_y: true
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      size: Member sequences
      origin: Origin
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: size

- component: table
  title: Protein family table
  description: |-
    Each row is a family with its origin, size, representative, seed, model and alignment statistics. It answers every number behind the tiles of this tab.
    How to read: sort by conservation or size to find families to inspect.
